clue.text: Go around in woman's clothing

definitions.meaning: to go around something is to avoid passing through it, as one does when bypassing a town
a garment hanging from the waist, worn chiefly by women

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to pass round the edge of something and a garment hanging from the waist.

clue.text: He may cause a sleeping partner to take action

definitions.text: He may cause a sleeping partner to take action

parts.words: He may cause a sleeping partner to take action
parts.note: a bedfellow kept awake by loud nocturnal breathing noises might nudge or kick the culprit; 'sleeping partner' plays on the business term for a silent investor

explanation.surface: A business note about a silent investor being spurred into activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who breathes noisily in sleep is the classic reason a bedmate elbows them awake.

clue.text: Take care, Gill reacts badly to certain things

definitions.note: an adjective here describing someone whose body reacts badly to certain substances

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are taken and remade, a loose instruction to rework them

explanation.surface: A warning to someone called Gill, who reacts badly to some things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' asks the solver to take the letters of CARE and GILL and rearrange them; 'reacts badly' looks like the anagram signal but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hypersensitive to pollen, nuts or similar substances suffers bad bodily reactions to them.

clue.text: The smallest matter in any study of body structure

indicators.note: the smallest matter is placed within the word any, which encloses it

parts.note: an atom is the smallest unit of a chemical element

explanation.surface: Physics meets biology: even the tiniest particles feature in a study of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of the body's structure, its organs and bones, is what medical students dissect for.

clue.text: 100 followed his violent riot-it was memorable

indicators.note: the hundred comes after the other pieces, which it follows
a violent riot is one in disorder, so its letters are thrown about

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A newspaper report of a man's riot that left a lasting mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violent' looks like it describes the riot but is the anagram signal; 'followed' sends the Roman numeral to the end, and 'it was' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something significant enough to be remembered in the record of the past.

clue.text: Give him a ring on the great day

definitions.text: Give him a ring on the great day

parts.words: Give him a ring on the great day
parts.note: reads as an instruction to telephone someone, but describes the wedding attendant who may hold the ring at the ceremony

explanation.surface: A reminder to phone a friend on his big day.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridegroom's attendant at a wedding often looks after the wedding band until it is needed.

clue.text: Hide a stone-from a miser perhaps?

parts.note: an animal's hide is its skin
flint is a hard grey stone

explanation.surface: Asking whether a hide and a stone could come from a stingy person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link here: the miser is the definition, with 'perhaps' marking it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight-fisted person is jokingly said to be so mean they would skin a flint.

clue.text: Lie about the material

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
re is Latin-derived for concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Someone tells untruths regarding the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A thread or substance from which cloth is made, such as cotton or nylon.

clue.text: To be cautious in the street is right

indicators.note: the clue places the abbreviation for right within the word for street

parts.note: a way is a road or street, as in many road names

explanation.surface: Advice that being careful when out on the road is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Being careful and watchful of danger is being on one's guard.

clue.text: Right, put about, nothing French is unclean

indicators.note: loosely signals that the French for nothing sits inside the word built so far
the word put goes round the abbreviation for right, surrounding it

explanation.surface: A fussy instruction set, ending with the claim that nothing French is dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions happen here: the abbreviation goes in after the first letter, and the French word goes in before the last. The setter's signal 'is' for the second one is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an unhealthy interest in sexual matters, so morally impure.

clue.text: Deed which involves mixing a tonic

indicators.note: mixing the letters as a barman might mix a drink

explanation.surface: Something done that involves preparing a gin and tonic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done, an act.

clue.text: Boast about clothes

indicators.note: turned about, so the word for clothes is read from its end back

explanation.surface: Someone showing off about their outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk big about oneself, to show off.

clue.text: Roy turns up in the dining room with a leading lady of the town

indicators.note: the pieces are placed within the word for a dining room

parts.note: a mess is a dining room in the armed forces

indicators.note: in a down-reading sense the name is inverted, read backwards

explanation.surface: Roy arrives at dinner escorting the town's first lady.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down-style reading 'turns up' means reversed. A mess is the dining room used by members of the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: The wife of a civic leader, or a woman holding that office, is the town's chief female citizen.

clue.text: Mistakenly ran to page for protection

indicators.note: done in error, so the letters end up in the wrong order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly hurried to a page boy for safety.
explanation.definitionFit: Support or sponsorship given by a powerful backer.

clue.text: Moved in a great hurry to fire rifle

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them from a job

explanation.surface: Someone dashed off to discharge a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like the gun but is the verb meaning to search and plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To search through and plunder, as burglars do a drawer.

clue.text: Eat pears cut up, on their own

indicators.note: fruit cut up into pieces, so the letters are chopped and rearranged

explanation.surface: A serving suggestion: slice the fruit and eat it plain.
explanation.definitionFit: Things kept apart, each by itself, rather than together.

clue.text: Outer garment which might be gloss

definitions.meaning: an overcoat worn over other clothes
the final layer of paint, which may well be a shiny finish

explanation.definitionFit: Both an overcoat and the final layer of paint applied to a surface.

clue.text: Decorate using ten Roman pieces

indicators.note: the words are broken into pieces and reassembled

explanation.surface: Adorning something with ten fragments of Roman pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to adorn or embellish.

clue.text: Bring the vegetables forward

parts.note: combines bringing something forward, to present it, with farm goods such as vegetables, both meanings of one word

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction to carry the greens to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to bring out or present and, as a noun, fruit and vegetables grown for sale.

clue.text: He intends to support Rose in some style

indicators.note: the name is put in a different style, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A man plans to back someone called Rose in grand fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in some style' rearranges the flower's name; 'Rose' looks like a person but is only fodder. The definition is an agent noun: one who puts forward an intention or a motion.
explanation.definitionFit: One who puts forward a plan or a marriage offer declares what he intends.

clue.text: Coming back just like me, not different

indicators.note: returning, so the short word for just like is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone returning who is exactly like the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming back' reverses only the short word meaning 'just like'; 'me' follows it unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical, alike in every respect.

clue.text: Tidings from all quarters

parts.note: the four compass points, north, east, west and south, as single letters

explanation.surface: Reports arriving from every direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings are information about recent events.

clue.text: Twisted round the curve in alarm

indicators.note: the word for twisted goes round the word for a curve

explanation.surface: A bent road around a bend causes panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A shout raised in battle, a call to arms that rouses the troops.

clue.text: Cry welcome!

definitions.meaning: in Scots dialect the word means to weep
to receive someone with a hello

explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish word for weeping, and the everyday verb for saying hello to someone.

clue.text: Bony cavity occupied by a worker with spirit

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A hollow in a bone is home to an insect with a bottle of liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: An anatomical term for a sinus or hollow within bone.

clue.text: Rare dame cooked with something sweet

indicators.note: cooked as food is, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An unusual lady cooked alongside a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A light brown cane sugar from Guyana.

clue.text: Silver tea set? No it's made of quartz

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Is this a silver tea service? No, it is quartz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea set' reads as one item but splits: 'set' is the anagram signal, and the 'No' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A banded semiprecious stone, a form of chalcedony, consists of microcrystalline quartz.

clue.text: Order naval shock to the Spanish by using underwater air lines

indicators.note: an order to rearrange, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: RN stands for the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Commanding a naval jolt to Spain by means of submarine breathing tubes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a naval command but signals an anagram; RN is the Royal Navy. This is an older spelling of the swimmer's breathing tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathing tube lets a swimmer or submarine draw air from the surface while submerged.
